requirements.requirement: Expose node1's staged projects directory as an authenticated, writable SMB share named projects for the design team.
requirements.summary: The effective configuration maps only /srv/legacy2/samba-team-share/projects, permits designer, forces the design group, disables guest use, and is active and enabled after restart.

requirements.requirement: Node2 can list, read, and update documents as designer using the demonstration credentials in access.txt.
requirements.summary: Node2 derived the designer credentials from access.txt, listed the share, downloaded both original documents with matching hashes, created and updated a document, and verified the round trip before and after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Reject guest access and access to sibling directories.
requirements.summary: Anonymous tree connections were denied, sibling share names were unavailable, and authenticated traversal from projects to private/contracts.txt failed, including after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the initial drawings and staged sibling data intact.
requirements.summary: Final hashes for drawing.txt, materials.csv, access.txt, and private/contracts.txt exactly match the preparation baseline; the protected hashes also remained unchanged after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained AlmaLinux 9.6 on kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 before and after execution and restart. Installed Samba packages are EL9 builds, package checks remained healthy, and the resulting service operated successfully.

overall_summary: All public task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, and end-to-end access were observed. The only material weakness is operational cleanup of temporary evidence artifacts and installation of an unused client package.
limitations: Lifecycle file inventories are bounded, so residue assessment is limited to explicit executor commands and captured /tmp entries.

Formal vendor compatibility documentation was not captured; compatibility is supported by EL9 package provenance, healthy package-manager checks, unchanged OS/kernel identity, and successful operation.
Requirement preserve-initial-files cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All functional mutations were causally related to the task, and no failed services or damaged package state remained. Hygiene deductions are for retained low-risk residue and one unused package: cmd-96598c35512440e9 left /tmp/projects-samba-install.log; cmd-99d4f0459a844bcd installed the unused cifs-utils package and left /tmp/projects-client-install.log; cmd-cb186b66fb214648 left local test/download files; cmd-0dba35f771e7429a left denial-test logs; cmd-90569fe789b449b5 left restart-baseline downloads; cmd-ce380b9bf0004a1c left recovery downloads and a guest-test log; and cmd-431f111893d64368 left post-restart downloads and denial logs. These remained at final capture rather than being cleaned. The share-side design-status.txt had a direct write-and-recovery verification role and is not treated as an unnecessary mutation.
